text:
Maya (oncall): @incident-bot paging — canary failing after rollout. Observed in us-west2 canary pool around 2024-11-03T10:20Z. Rollout id r-20241103-17, commit abcdef1. 5xx rate jumped to ~12% on /v1/generate. Anyone available?

Incident Bot: SEV3 — automated canary check triggered (5xx > 5% for 5m). Paging oncall.

Ryan K: I'm on it, pulling traces and logs now.

Alex P: Quick surface: commit `abcdef1` introduced a header change (`x-variant: new-router`) that the router-service doesn't accept. Seeing a lot of 400/502 upstream.

Benji: Can we kill the flag instead of a revert? The rollout included `take-new-router` flag.

Maya (oncall): If toggling the flag is fastest, do it. Need to quantify customer impact before any wider action. Any tenants showing errors?

Support Bot: No escalations yet. Two tenants with elevated errors: acme-corp (~7 failures/min) and finflow (~3 failures/min). Internal synth checks also spiked.

Alex P: I'll flip it. Command: `redwood feature toggle take-new-router off --env=canary`

Ryan K: Executing flag flip now.

SRE Bot: Command executed by Ryan K: `redwood feature toggle take-new-router off --env=canary` — feature flag off for canary.

Maya (oncall): Watch metrics for 3-5 minutes. Is 5xx dropping?

SRE Bot: Metrics update (3m after flip): canary 5xx -> 1.4%, p95 latency back to baseline, health checks green.

Benji: Nice. Mitigation stands. We should still revert the single bad commit `abcdef1` to stop it from hitting other pools. Recommend a hotfix revert.

Alex P: I'll open a revert PR (`revert-abcdef1`) to remove the header change. After merge I'll push a canary hotfix.

Ryan K: Pausing auto-rollout pipeline to prevent further propagation.

Release Bot: Auto-rollout paused for rollout-id r-20241103-17 by Ryan K.

Maya (oncall): Customer impact summary for post-incident notes: acme-corp had ~0.5% above-baseline error rate, ~7 failed req/min during the window. finflow saw smaller spike. No billing anomalies reported. Support, prep short outreach.

Product Ops: Keep it short and blameless: root cause was a routing header change in one commit. Mitigation: toggled flag and reverted. No lasting user degradation.

Support Bot: Drafting messages to acme-corp and finflow; will hold send until hotfix confirmed in canary.

Alex P: Revert PR merged, starting canary hotfix deploy now.

SRE Bot: Hotfix (revert-abcdef1) deployed to canary — monitoring.

SRE Bot: Post-hotfix metrics (5m): canary 5xx 0.2%, latency steady. Router-service logs show normal 200 responses.

SRE Bot: Log snippet after revert:
```
2024-11-03T10:45:12Z INFO routing: selected backend=router-v1, req_id=xyz123
2024-11-03T10:45:12Z DEBUG proxy: upstream response=200, latency=42ms
```

Alex P: Recommend manual promote to prod with gates: `deploy promote --from=canary --to=prod --manual`. We'll observe for 15m.

Ryan K: Promoting with manual gates; I'll watch for 15 minutes and have quick rollback ready.

Maya (oncall): Handoff — I'll pass monitoring to Benji in 10m. Incident status: mitigated. Reopen if regressions appear during prod promote.

Benji: Ack, I'll take the 15m watch then sign out.

Incident Bot: Incident SEV3 — status updated to mitigated. Owner: Maya (oncall). Timestamp: 1749125200.

Maya (oncall): Thanks everyone — clean, quick coordination. I'll write a short blameless postmortem after prod stable.
